page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter · 2 marks

steps.label: The relation
lines: Every moving particle has a wave associated
with it, called a matter wave or a de Broglie
wave. The wavelength of this wave is
steps.margin_note: First mark. One sentence for the hypothesis, then the relation λ = h/mv.
steps.why: Light shows both wave and particle behaviour. De Broglie proposed the same duality for matter: a particle of momentum p moves with an associated wave of wavelength h/p.
common_mistakes: Writing λ = h·mv. Momentum divides Planck's constant; a faster or heavier particle has a SHORTER wavelength.
Applying the relation only to electrons. It holds for every moving particle.

recall.must_convey: That every moving particle has a matter wave with wavelength lambda equals h by m v.
accept: lambda equals h by m v

steps.memory_tip: Constant over momentum: λ = h/p, so more momentum means less wavelength.

steps.label: Meaning of each term
lines: Here λ is the de Broglie wavelength of the
particle, h is Planck's constant, m is the
mass of the particle, v is its speed, and
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name every symbol: λ, h, m, v and p.
steps.why: The question asks for the terms by name, so each of the five symbols needs its own words — the wavelength, the constant, the mass, the speed, the momentum.
common_mistakes: Skipping p = mv. The book writes both forms, and naming p costs one short phrase.
Calling v the velocity of light. Here v is the speed of the particle; c belongs to photons.

recall.must_convey: That lambda is the wavelength, h is Planck's constant, m the mass, v the speed and p = mv the momentum of the particle.
accept: m is the mass and v is the speed
reject: lambda equals h by m v

steps.memory_tip: Five symbols to name: λ, h, m, v, p — count them off as you write.

insider_note: State the hypothesis in one sentence before the formula — the relation without the words matter wave reads as half an answer.
